chapters.label: THE WALK
chapters.title: One waterfall, several useful angles
chapters.body: Tad Yuang drops roughly 40 metres and can be read from more than one level. Paths and stairs connect viewpoints around the top and lower section, so the visit has a natural progression: see the shape from above, descend for a closer perspective, then decide whether the extra climb is worth your time.

chapters.label: THE PAIRING
chapters.title: Why it works beside Tad Fane
chapters.body: Tad Fane gives you distance and scale; Tad Yuang gives you movement and proximity. That contrast is enough reason to visit both without turning the day into a waterfall checklist. If you are cutting stops, choose according to the experience you want rather than the name you have heard more often.

note.label: USEFUL CHOICE
note.text: Short on time? Tad Fane for the panorama; Tad Yuang for the walk.

items.label: Time needed
items.detail: That gives you time for more than the top viewpoint and keeps the descent from becoming a race.

items.label: Walking
items.detail: The lower viewpoints require a descent and climb back. Wet-season surfaces can be slippery.

items.label: Conditions
items.value: Powerful wet season · easier walking in drier months
items.detail: Choose between stronger flow and more comfortable trail conditions rather than assuming one season is simply better.

items.label: Entry
items.detail: Use the current gate price; old online fee references age quickly.

faq.question: How is Tad Yuang different from Tad Fane?
faq.answer: Tad Yuang is a more physical on-site visit, with paths and several viewpoints around the fall. Tad Fane is primarily about seeing a much deeper twin waterfall gorge from across the rim.

faq.question: How long should I spend at Tad Yuang?
faq.answer: Allow one to two hours if you want to use the lower viewpoints rather than stopping only at the top.

faq.question: Can I combine Tad Yuang and Tad Fane?
faq.answer: Yes. They are close enough to work naturally in the same Bolaven Plateau outing, and the two experiences are different enough to avoid feeling repetitive.

faq.question: Is Tad Yuang difficult to walk?
faq.answer: The visit is straightforward for most people who are comfortable with stairs, but the descent means a climb back out and the surfaces can become slippery in wet weather.

faq.question: Can you swim at Tad Yuang?
faq.answer: There is water at the base, but conditions change with flow and weather. Do not plan the visit around swimming; judge the site on the day and follow any local restrictions.
